metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: Asking profound, difficult, or existential questions about one's life and deeds.
acceptable_visual_variants: A soul standing before Yamraj with hands folded in deep contemplation
A soul looking upward with a questioning, serious expression
metaphor_spans.literal_meaning: asked physically deep or bottomless questions
metaphor_spans.literalization_risk: An illustrator might depict physical questions or words sinking into a deep pit or water, which would look bizarre and miss the intellectual nature of the inquiry.

transferred_attributes: difficult to reach the bottom of

metaphor_spans.tenor: intellectual or existential profundity of the questions
metaphor_spans.vehicle: physical depth (like a deep well or ocean)
metaphor_spans.visualization_strategy: Depict souls with thoughtful, intense, or searching facial expressions while addressing Yamraj in his court.

metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: Revealing hidden truths, sins, or secrets of one's past life.
acceptable_visual_variants: A soul speaking with open palms facing upward
A soul bowing head in confession before the court
metaphor_spans.literal_meaning: opened physical locks or containers of old secrets
metaphor_spans.literalization_risk: Showing souls physically opening boxes or chests labeled 'secrets' would look overly literal and cartoonish.
metaphor_spans.tenor: disclosing hidden personal truths or memories
metaphor_spans.vehicle: opening a physical container or unrolling a scroll
metaphor_spans.visualization_strategy: Depict a soul gesturing with open hands, as if laying bare their heart or speaking transparently, with a look of relief or confession.

translation_loss.what_was_lost: The Urdu-derived term 'mahfil' (gathering/court) carries a specific cultural nuance of an intimate, poetic, or musical gathering, which is flattened into the more formal and generic English word 'assembly'.

metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: Yamraj, the god of death who is traditionally feared, acting with comforting, gentle, and friendly benevolence toward the souls.
acceptable_visual_variants: Yamraj smiling warmly from his seat with a hand raised in a blessing or comforting gesture
Yamraj looking down at a soul with kind, compassionate eyes
metaphor_spans.literal_meaning: as if he were literally a personal companion or friend to everyone
metaphor_spans.literalization_risk: Depicting Yamraj casually hanging out, high-fiving, or embracing souls like modern friends would undermine the solemnity and majesty of his divine role.
metaphor_spans.source_span_translation: As if he were a friend to each
metaphor_spans.visualization_strategy: Show Yamraj with a gentle, warm, and reassuring smile, leaning slightly forward with a comforting hand gesture toward the souls, balancing majesty with kindness.

translation_loss.what_was_lost: The shift from the continuous past tense 'muskurate rahe' (kept smiling) to the simple past participle 'deta' (giving/offering) in the original Hindi creates a subtle aspectual shift that is flattened into a standard participle 'Offering' in English.

metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: The clarity and revealing power of absolute truth that makes everything clear and undeniable.
acceptable_visual_variants: A warm, ambient divine glow illuminating the entire court scene
Beams of soft light descending from above onto the gathered souls
metaphor_spans.literal_meaning: inside the physical electromagnetic radiation emitted by truth
metaphor_spans.literalization_risk: Depicting a literal lightbulb or a spotlight labeled 'truth' shining on people would look cheap and overly literal.
metaphor_spans.tenor: the revealing and clarifying power of truth
metaphor_spans.visualization_strategy: Use a soft, ethereal, golden or white divine glow emanating from the center of the assembly or from Yamraj himself, illuminating the faces of the souls clearly.

metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: Seeing one's true self, moral character, and the reality of one's past deeds clearly without any self-deception.
acceptable_visual_variants: A soul looking at their own glowing hands or chest with an expression of sudden understanding
A soul looking into a calm pool of water in front of Yamraj's throne, seeing their life's deeds reflected
metaphor_spans.literal_meaning: saw their physical reflection as if in a mirror
metaphor_spans.literalization_risk: Showing souls holding physical hand mirrors or looking into a glass mirror would distract from the spiritual nature of self-reckoning.
metaphor_spans.visualization_strategy: Depict souls looking down at their own hands or looking inward with expressions of deep realization, shock, or peace as they recognize their true nature.

metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: An environment where only truth existed and no falsehood or deception could survive.
acceptable_visual_variants: A clean, majestic, and luminous court hall design
An open-air assembly under a clear, starry or luminous sky
metaphor_spans.literal_meaning: truth was a physical person living as a resident in the hall

metaphor_spans.visualization_strategy: Create an atmosphere of absolute clarity, order, and solemnity in the court, free of shadows, clutter, or chaotic elements, symbolizing pure truth.

translation_loss.what_was_lost: The Persian-derived word 'aks' (reflection/shadow) carries a poetic depth and visual precision in Urdu/Hindi poetry that is rendered as the more literal and common English word 'reflection'.

metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: Feeling completely purified, unburdened, and spiritually renewed after facing judgment and truth.
acceptable_visual_variants: Souls walking away toward a bright horizon with light steps and peaceful smiles
Souls depicted with translucent, glowing bodies looking up at a bright sky with hope
metaphor_spans.literal_meaning: as if they literally died and were physically born as infants again on the spot
metaphor_spans.literalization_risk: Depicting souls turning into physical babies or crawling out of wombs would be highly inappropriate and literalistic.
metaphor_spans.visualization_strategy: Depict the souls leaving the assembly with light, floating postures, glowing with a soft inner light, and carrying expressions of profound peace, relief, and joy.

translation_loss.what_was_lost: The phrase 'naya janm paya' literally means 'obtained a new birth' or 'attained rebirth', which carries strong cultural and spiritual resonance of reincarnation in Indian philosophy, slightly softened by the English passive/adjectival rendering 'reborn anew'.

annotation.theme: The transition of souls in the court of Yamraj, where self-reflection and truth lead to ultimate solace and rebirth

original_poem:
यमराज की महफ़िल में,  
हर आत्मा थी मेहमान,  
कुछ ने सवाल किए गहरे,  
कुछ ने खोले पुराने राज़।  

यमराज मुस्कुराते रहे,  
अपने अधिकार में शांति से,  
हर एक को देता सांत्वना,  
जैसे वह सबका मित्र हो।  

सच्चाई की रोशनी में,  
सभी ने देखा अपना अक्स,  
यमराज की महफ़िल में,  
सिर्फ सच का ही था वास।  

जब रात ढली अंत में,  
सभी ने पाया अपना मार्ग,  
यमराज की महफ़िल से लौटे,  
जैसे कोई नया जन्म पाया।
translated_poem:
In Yamraj's assembly,  
Every soul was a guest,  
Some asked deep questions,  
Some revealed old secrets.  

Yamraj kept smiling,  
Calm in his authority,  
Offering solace to all,  
As if he were a friend to each.  

In the light of truth,  
Everyone saw their reflection,  
In Yamraj's assembly,  
Only truth had residence.  

When the night finally waned,  
Each soul found its path,  
Returning from Yamraj's assembly,  
As if reborn anew.
